**Andrew Cuomo's resignation**
Cuomo, governor of New York from 2011, resigned in August 2021 after a report by state Attorney General Letitia James found he had sexually harassed multiple women, including former aides Lindsey Boylan and Charlotte Bennett. He was also criticized for undercounting COVID-19 deaths in New York nursing homes.

**2021 New York City mayoral election and ranked-choice voting**
The first major NYC race to use ranked-choice voting, held to replace the term-limited Bill de Blasio. In the Democratic primary, Kathryn Garcia and Andrew Yang campaigned together against front-runner Eric Adams, and other candidates included Maya Wiley, Scott Stringer (accused of sexual misconduct by Jean Kim), Dianne Morales (whose campaign imploded), and rapper Paperboy Prince. The Board of Elections embarrassingly included about 135,000 test ballots in an early ranked-choice tally.

**Eric Adams**
A former NYPD captain and Brooklyn Borough President who won the 2021 mayoral race. During the campaign, questions about whether he really lived in the city included a widely mocked reporter's look at salmon in his refrigerator. In 2024 he was indicted on federal bribery charges, his police commissioner Edward Caban resigned after federal agents seized phones from city officials, and Tom Donlon became interim commissioner.

**"Thursday Night Massacre"**
In February 2025, acting Southern District of New York U.S. Attorney Danielle Sassoon and several other Justice Department prosecutors, seven in all, resigned rather than obey Trump administration orders to drop the corruption case against Mayor Eric Adams. The case was later dismissed.

**Curtis Sliwa**
The founder of the Guardian Angels, a volunteer anti-crime patrol group, known for his red beret and his apartment full of rescued cats. He beat Fernando Mateo in the 2021 Republican primary and was the party's nominee for mayor in 2021 and 2025. He has described being shot in a taxi in 1992 in an attack linked to the Gotti family of the Gambino crime family.

**Zohran Mamdani and the 2025 mayoral election**
A democratic socialist state assemblyman from Queens who won the 2025 Democratic primary, helped by ranked-choice cross-endorsements with Comptroller Brad Lander, and defeated Andrew Cuomo, who ran as an independent, in the general election. His viral street-interview campaign videos included one on "Halalflation," the rising price of halal street food. He took office in January 2026 with a swearing-in at the disused City Hall subway station.

**Kathy Hochul**
A Buffalo-area Democrat who won a 2011 special election for Congress, later became lieutenant governor, and became New York's first female governor when Cuomo resigned in 2021. The state Senate rejected her 2023 nominee for chief judge, Hector LaSalle, over concerns about his record on abortion and labor, and she then appointed Rowan Wilson.

**George Santos**
A Republican congressman from New York's 3rd district on Long Island whose biography turned out to be largely fabricated. He was indicted on federal fraud charges, including the 23-count superseding indictment, and expelled from the House in December 2023. Reports also revealed he had performed in drag in Brazil under the name "Kitara Ravache."

**Elise Stefanik**
A Republican representative from upstate New York who replaced Liz Cheney as House Republican Conference Chair in 2021. At a December 2023 hearing on campus antisemitism, her questioning led UPenn president Liz Magill to say that calls for the genocide of Jews might violate policy depending on "context," and Magill resigned days later.

**Buffalo Tops supermarket shooting**
In May 2022, white supremacist Payton Gendron, motivated by the "Great Replacement" conspiracy theory, killed 10 Black people at a Tops supermarket in Buffalo and livestreamed the attack on Twitch. Other Buffalo clues include police shoving 75-year-old protester Martin Gugino in 2020, the Elmwood Avenue Starbucks becoming the first to unionize in 2021, and Mayor Byron Brown winning a write-in campaign after losing the Democratic primary to socialist India Walton.

**Columbia University protests**
In April 2024, President Nemat "Minouche" Shafik called in police to clear a pro-Palestinian encampment on Columbia's Manhattan campus, and protesters later occupied Hamilton Hall. Shafik resigned in August 2024, and administrators were forced out over "Textgate," leaked texts that mocked a discussion of antisemitism.

**Frank James subway shooting**
In April 2022, Frank James set off smoke grenades and shot passengers on an N train in Sunset Park, Brooklyn. Police identified him using keys to a rented U-Haul van left at the scene, and he was later sentenced to life in prison.

**Letitia James**
New York's Attorney General since 2019. Besides producing the investigation that led to Cuomo's resignation, she filed a 2020 lawsuit seeking to dissolve the National Rifle Association over financial misconduct by its leaders.

**Sheldon Silver and Dean Skelos**
Silver, longtime Speaker of the New York State Assembly, and Skelos, Senate Majority Leader, were both convicted of corruption in 2015. Their cases involved firms such as the real estate developer Glenwood Management and were seen as symbols of "Albany" corruption.

**Marriage Equality Act**
The 2011 law, signed by newly elected Governor Andrew Cuomo after he defeated Tea Party-backed Carl Paladino, that legalized same-sex marriage in New York. It passed the State Senate on June 24, 2011.
